definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese sliding door or room divider made of a wooden frame covered with thick paper or cloth.

examples.english: I opened the sliding screen and went into the next room.

examples.english: I had the old fusuma re-papered.
The painting on the fusuma was done by a famous artist.

examples.english: When you close the fusuma in the Japanese-style room, you can hardly hear the sounds from the next room.

notes:
{襖|ふすま} are traditional Japanese sliding doors used as room dividers in Japanese-style rooms. Unlike ⟦{障子|しょうじ}→障子：04201_shouji⟧, they are opaque.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {襖|ふすま}: Opaque sliding screen (thick paper/cloth)
- ⟦{障子|しょうじ}→障子：04201_shouji⟧: Translucent sliding screen (thin paper that lets light through)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {襖|ふすま}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧ (to open the fusuma)
- {襖|ふすま}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{閉|し}める→閉める：00485_shimeru⟧ (to close the fusuma)
- {襖|ふすま}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{張|は}り{替|か}える→張り替える：28418_harikaeru⟧ (to re-paper the fusuma)
- ⟦{襖絵|ふすまえ}→襖絵：29410_fusumae⟧ (painting on fusuma)

CULTURAL NOTE:
{襖|ふすま} can feature elaborate paintings and are sometimes valuable works of art, especially in ⟦{寺|てら}→寺：01676_tera⟧ and historic buildings.
